column1: # Reference set -- raghavendra_2023_ecoli
# Single-organism 10 pg E. coli libraries from
#   Basapathi Raghavendra J, Zorzano M-P, Kumaresan D, Martin-Torres J.
#   "DNA sequencing at the picogram level to investigate life on Mars and Earth."
# Reads: https://zenodo.org/records/8208597 ("MinION low detectability.zip"),
# fetched by comparison/fetch_raghavendra.sh.
# Covers Ec_R1 / Ec_R2 / Ec_R3, the paper's Table 2 row
# "10 pg of E. coli lenticule discs extract".
# WHY THIS EXISTS
# This is not our data. It is a re-analysis of a prior study's deposited reads
# under THIS pipeline's competitive-mapping assignment, so that the prior study
# can be compared like-for-like against our numbers instead of Kraken2-against-
# PlusPF-8 versus minimap2-against-a-known-reference. See comparison/README.md.
# NO CARRIER
# Raghavendra et al. used no genomic carrier. Methods, "Library preparation":
# "The gDNA for the nanopore library was prepared using nuclease-free water and
# the low concentration of the DNA to be tested was directly pipetted from the
# previously diluted samples" and "The whole amount of DNA ... was diluted in
# 25 ul for library preparation", with SQK-LSK114 at halved reagent volumes on
# an R10.4.1 Flongle. Nothing anywhere in the paper adds lambda or any other
# filler DNA. There is therefore no role=carrier row here and carrier_dna_ng=0
# in the samplesheet, which makes input_sample_fraction = 1.0 and enrichment
# = output_sample_fraction (i.e. enrichment is not a meaningful quantity for
# this study -- only the per-fg yields are).
# ACCESSION CHOICE -- Escherichia coli, GCA_900706755.1
# Methods, "Test samples": "Escherichia coli (NCTC 9001 Lenticule disc, Sigma
# Aldrich, UK) with an average genomic size of ~ 5 Mb". NCTC 9001 is a named
# strain, and it was sequenced by the Sanger Institute's NCTC 3000 project
# (BioProject PRJEB6403, BioSample SAMEA2517362, assembly 27731_A01):
# 5.04 Mb corroborates the paper's stated "~5 Mb". This is the exact strain, so
# it is preferred over a generic K-12 reference; lowinput_s1.tsv sets the same
# precedent of taking a contig-level assembly when it is the exact strain.
# NOTE the GenBank (GCA_) accession is deliberate: the paired RefSeq assembly
# GCF_900706755.1 is SUPPRESSED, so `datasets download genome accession` cannot
# retrieve it. bin/build_reference_set.py and main.nf both accept GC[AF]_.
# HOMO SAPIENS IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT
# The paper reports human reads in every sample and in the negative controls
# (Table 2: 0-2 human reads here; Table 3: up to 53). Human is nevertheless not
# included as a contaminant reference, for two reasons. (1) Cost: the pipeline
# fetches and indexes references once per reference set, and this study needs
# four sets, so GRCh38 would be downloaded and indexed four times. (2) Direction
# of the error: adding a competitor to a competitive assignment can only move
# reads AWAY from E. coli / S. cerevisiae, never toward them, so omitting human
# makes these counts an UPPER BOUND on the prior study -- the conservative
# direction with respect to any advantage we claim. Unmapped human reads land in
# the `unassigned` bin, which compute_metrics.py reconciles explicitly, so they
# are visible rather than lost. To account for them instead, add:
#   Homo sapiens<TAB>GCF_000001405.40<TAB>contaminant<TAB>0<TAB>GRCh38.p14<TAB>documented cross-contamination
# theoretical_dna_fraction: single-organism library, so 1.0 by construction.
organism
Escherichia coli
column6: contig-level (5 contigs) exact strain named in Methods; 5,040,580 bp
